item.title: Argentina temporarily closes Iguazu Falls after El Niño-fuelled surge in water levels
item.description:
National park officials took the precautionary measure to limit tourist access after heavy rain caused the Iguazu River to flow at six times the normal rate

Heavy rainfall fuelled by a supersized El Niño weather pattern briefly forced Argentinian authorities to close tourist access to the famed Iguazu Falls, amid fears that rapidly rising water levels would cause the river to burst its banks.

National park officials took the precautionary measure on Monday when the Iguazu River’s flow exceeded 12,000 cubic metres per second – more than six times its average rate.

item.title: The billion-dollar shipwreck and the man who tried to find it – podcast
item.description:
Journalist Julian Sancton on the story of the most valuable shipwreck in history and who could end up with its treasures

A few years ago, the journalist Julian Sancton came across a story about a shipwreck found off the coast of Colombia. Onboard were treasures supposedly worth $1bn – which, he thought, must’ve been a typo. But it wasn’t. “It was supposedly billions, many tons, more than 100 tons of gold and silver,” he told Michael Safi.

He wrote a piece for Vanity Fair about the extraordinary 300-year mystery of where this ship had sunk, and how it had been finally found a decade ago. But the more Julian dug into the story, the more he realised that the tale of the man who had done more than anyone to find the San José was just as tantalising.

item.title: Fugitive businessman taken into US custody in Venezuela bribery case
item.description:
A businessman wanted in the US for allegedly bribing top Venezuelan officials has been taken into custody

A businessman wanted for years in the US for allegedly paying bribes to top Venezuelan officials in exchange for lucrative state contracts in Venezuela has been taken into custody.

Alvaro Pulido was indicted in Miami federal court in 2019 and again in 2021 as part of an investigation into his longtime business partner, Alex Saab, a one-time ally of ousted Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro. The US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and the state department had been offering a reward of up to $10m for information leading to his arrest.

item.title: Two Years On, the Sinaloa Cartel War Changes Shape | The InSight Take
item.description:
Two Years On, the Sinaloa Cartel War Changes Shape | The InSight Take

Two years after Ismael Zambada Garcia, alias "El Mayo," was handed over to US authorities in what was deemed a traitorous act by one faction against another, the war between the Chapitos and the Mayiza factions of the Sinaloa Cartel continues to roil the area. The conflict has implications for the criminal superstructure throughout the country.

InSight Crime's Victoria Dittmar and co-director Steven Dudley were recently in Culiacán, Sinaloa, where they interviewed drug producers, residents, and local sources. They found a city where the war is less visible than it was but no less present.
